intro.title: Portal
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple modal dialog that renders outside the main Vue app's DOM hierarchy using a portal. You will learn the core concept of portals, which allow you to render a component's content at a different location in the DOM while preserving its Vue reactivity and event handling. The main technologies involved are Vue's built-in Teleport component and basic Vue single-file components with template syntax. This beginner-friendly project will help you understand how to manage UI elements like modals, tooltips, or notifications that need to break out of parent CSS constraints.
intro.usecase: Portals are essential for managing UI elements that need to break out of their parent component's DOM hierarchy while maintaining Vue's reactivity and component context. You'll use portals for modals, tooltips, and dropdown menus that must render at the document root to avoid CSS clipping or z-index conflicts. In complex applications like dashboards with floating panels or e-commerce sites with persistent shopping carts, portals ensure these overlay components remain accessible and properly positioned. This pattern is particularly valuable when building design systems or component libraries where UI elements need predictable rendering regardless of where they're used in the component tree.
